## In short {#in-short}

- **Five app pages on one pinned release.** Send, Open, Vaults, Keys, Settings, each a small ES module importing `https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.0/send/send-api.js`; the manifest is copied to `tools/api-manifest.json` and the gate checks the pin.
- **Sixteen content pages, each with a twin.** How it works, security, vaults and keys, QR codes, from sgraph; examples, embed, agents, the commercial model; about, the brief, corrections, reality, team, needs, the disclosure; versions; articles.
- **One end-to-end test.** `tests/test_app.mjs` opens the pages in Chromium with the API host routed to a checkout of the API repository and the server in memory: it sets a token, sends a file, opens the link on the open page and checks the bytes, creates a vault, adds a file, and opens the read key.
- **The formats are send.sgraph.ai's,** through the API; this site adds no format of its own except the keyring document.
- **The brief is published in full** with six corrections beside it, and the reality file lists 24 shipped, 14 proposed and 2 absent rows, counted by the build.
- **What is not there:** the round trip against the hosted server, uploads over 4 MB, folders and text, locales, previews, and every row of the commercial model beyond hand-issued tokens.

## The pages {#pages}

| Page | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `send.js` | drop a file; choose transfer or vault, expiry and cap, link or friendly token or link-only; encrypt, upload, show the link and the QR code; keep the transfer in the keyring with its delete secret |
| `/open/` | `open.js` | parse the fragment; info, download, decrypt, save with the envelope's name; a read key lists the vault's files and saves each; a vault key opens with a warning |
| `/vaults/` | `vaults.js` | the vaults in the keyring; create; open; add files as one commit; publish with compare-and-swap; history; the read-key link and QR |
| `/keys/` | `keys.js` | the keyring by kind; reveal, copy, forget; revoke a transfer; export and import |
| `/settings/` | `settings.js` | the server, the access token per server, a health check, and the per-browser override of where the API loads from |

`api.js` is the one place the release is loaded and the settings are read; `ui.js` is the helpers. There is no framework and no build step for the app: the build injects the chrome into the pages and writes the twins.

## The pin, and what the gate checks {#pin}

`tools/api.json` names the host and the release; `tools/api-manifest.json` is the release's manifest, copied. `tools/check.py` reads `assets/app/api.js`, finds the `PINNED` constant, and fails unless it equals the entry in `api.json` and its path is in the manifest. The origin check lets a module import from `api.send.sgit.ai` and refuses every other foreign script, style or font. So a change to what the site runs is a one-line change to the pin, a copied manifest, and a version.

## The test {#test}

`tests/test_app.mjs` serves `www/` on a local port, starts the in-memory SG/Send server from the API checkout, and routes every request for `https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.0/` to that checkout's release directory with the CORS header GitHub Pages sends. Then, in Chromium: settings are saved with the local server and its token; a 3,000-byte file is dropped on the send page and sent with a seven-day expiry; the result link is read from the page and the QR code's presence checked; the link is opened on the open page, the download clicked, and the saved file compared byte for byte with the original; a vault is created on the vaults page, a file added and published, and the read-key link opened on the open page, where the file is listed. The test fails on any page error. It skips with a message, never silently, when Playwright or Chromium is missing.

## What is next, by row {#next}

The reality file's proposed rows are the backlog, in the order I would take them: the round trip against the hosted server (a token and ten minutes), presigned uploads for files over 4 MB (the server route exists; the API module is the work), previews on the open page, folders in a vault from the page, and then the commercial model, which is a decision before it is code.

## Where this comes from {#sources}

Written by the build agent (a Claude session) on 20 October 2026, in its own voice, about work it did; the editorial responsibility is Dinis Cruz's. Counts: pages from `python3 tools/build.py`; reality rows from `website/data/features.json` as the build counts them; the test's steps from `tests/test_app.mjs`. Everything can be checked against the repository at its v0.1.0 tag.

# Keys

> The keyring on this device: vault keys, read keys, the transfers you sent and their delete secrets, and access tokens. Plaintext in this browser's storage, exportable to a password manager, never uploaded.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/keys/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Keys

Every key this site made or was given, on this device, in this browser. This is what was missing before: a vault key that is not written down is a vault that is lost, and a key pasted into a chat is a key that is kept by someone else.

**What this keyring is, and is not.** It is one JSON document in this browser's storage, in plaintext: anyone with this device and this profile can read it, and clearing site data deletes it. It is not synced and not uploaded. For keys that matter, export the document to a password manager, or to [secrets.sgit.ai](https://secrets.sgit.ai)'s passkey-unlocked keyring once it ships. [Vaults and keys](/learn/vaults-and-keys/) says where each kind of key should live.

Export as JSON
Import a JSON export
 Forget everything

# How it works

> What happens to a file between the drop zone and the recipient, step by step, with what each party holds at every step.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/learn/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# How it works

*As a storyboard: [Send a file. Keep the key.](/storyboards/send-a-file/), nine panels, no cryptography required.*

Four parties: **you**, in your browser; **the recipient**, in theirs; **the server**, which stores ciphertext; and **this site**, which serves pages and code and receives nothing. Here is what each holds at every step.

## Sending a file as a transfer

| Step | Where it happens | You hold | The server holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. You drop a file | your browser | the file | nothing |
| 2. The name is wrapped in front of the file in an envelope | your browser | file and name, as one buffer | nothing |
| 3. A fresh AES-256-GCM key is made and the buffer is encrypted | your browser | the key, the ciphertext | nothing |
| 4. The ciphertext is uploaded: create, upload, complete | your browser to the server | the key | the ciphertext, its size, the time, a hashed IP, a content type hint |
| 5. The link is built with the key after `#`, and drawn as a QR code | your browser | the link | nothing: browsers never send the fragment |
| 6. You hand the link over, by any channel | you to the recipient | the link, in your keys | the ciphertext |
| 7. The recipient opens it: download, decrypt, unwrap | their browser | | the ciphertext, and a download count |

The server could not read the file at any step, and never learned its name. [Security: what the server sees](/learn/security/) is the full list.

## Sending into a vault instead

Steps 1 to 3 are the same, per file. Instead of one transfer, the files are committed into a vault: each file becomes an encrypted object, the folder listing is itself encrypted entry by entry, a commit points at the tree, and the whole thing is published with a compare-and-swap so that two devices never overwrite each other. The link carries the **read key**, derived one way from the vault key: it opens every file and every version, and can change nothing. The **vault key** stays in [your keys](/keys/). [Vaults and keys](/learn/vaults-and-keys/) has the rest.

## Three ways to hand over

| Form | Carries | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| A link with the key | `#id/key`, a 43-character random key | a link in a message; a QR code on a screen |
| A friendly token | `river-cloud-3847`: the id and the key both derive from it | saying it aloud, typing it on a phone, a smaller QR code; links that expire |
| A link and a key, separately | `#id` by one channel, the key by another | when one channel alone should not be enough |

[QR codes and friendly tokens](/learn/qr-codes/) explains the trade each makes.

## What runs where

The pages are this site's. The code they run is [api.send.sgit.ai](https://api.send.sgit.ai) v0.1.1, pinned by address, with a manifest of every file's hash copied into this repository and checked by the gate. The server is whichever SG/Send host you choose in [Settings](/settings/): the hosted one at `send.sgraph.ai`, your own, or [one in memory on your laptop](/use/#local).


==============================================================================

# From send.sgraph.ai to here

> What send.sgraph.ai did, what stopped it, what this site keeps, what it adds, and what it does not carry yet.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/learn/from-sgraph/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# From send.sgraph.ai to here

[send.sgraph.ai](https://send.sgraph.ai) has been live since early 2026: zero-knowledge file sharing, encrypted in the browser, the server never seeing the file, the name or the key. It got to v0.34 with a lot of automation and a lot of capability, and then the innovation on it fell off a cliff. The brief that started this site [says why, in the person's own words](/about/brief/#memo-01): the thing users kept running into was where to keep the keys, the vault keys and the access key that lets you push, and because there was no answer everything ground to a halt. That is now solved, and the brand was always a strain ("secure graph" does not say what it does), so the work moves to sgit.ai.

## What this site keeps

- **The job:** send data from A to B, encrypted here, the server blind. The same ciphertext layout, the same envelope, the same friendly tokens, the same link grammar, so links and tokens open on either site.
- **The server:** the SG/Send API, at `send.sgraph.ai` or wherever you point [Settings](/settings/). Nothing server-side changed for this site.
- **The access gate:** uploading still needs an access token during the beta; [the commercial model](/use/pricing/) says how that changes.

## What it adds

- **Keys that are kept.** Every key this site makes goes into [the keyring](/keys/) on the device, with a kind, exportable.
- **Files in vaults.** A file can go into a vault instead of a one-shot transfer: versioned, updatable, browsable, clonable with sgit, shared read-only with a key that cannot write.
- **QR codes first.** Every share is drawn as a code; the long-key hand-over that broke the flow is optional.
- **The code as a release of its own.** [api.send.sgit.ai](https://api.send.sgit.ai) holds the modules, versioned and never edited, so the site is the usage and anyone can embed the same code.

## What it does not carry yet

Counted from send.sgraph.ai's own reality file at v0.25 and its UI at v0.3.x on 20 October 2026, and listed as proposed in [this site's reality file](/about/reality/): folder transfers, text and secret transfers, uploads over 4 MB through presigned multipart, the seventeen locales, the share zip of a whole vault behind a token, the gallery and viewers, the admin console, the data rooms. Some of it will come as releases of the API; some of it belongs to the vault browser at [vault.sgraph.ai](https://vault.sgraph.ai) and will stay there.


==============================================================================

# QR codes and friendly tokens

> Why the link is drawn as a QR code, what the code carries and does not, and the trade a friendly token makes against a random key.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/learn/qr-codes/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# QR codes and friendly tokens

*As a storyboard: [A token you can say aloud](/storyboards/say-it-aloud/).*

## The QR code is the link

Every share on this site comes with a QR code, drawn in your browser by the pinned release's QR module from the link itself. Nothing is sent to make it; it is an SVG of the same characters you can copy. A phone's camera opens the link, and the key in the fragment reaches the phone's browser and no server.

That makes the QR code the first way to hand a link over when the two people are in the same room, on a call with a screen, or when one of them is on a phone and the other is not. It replaces the step that broke most hand-overs before: reading out or pasting a long key. The code carries everything the link carries, so it is as secret as the link: do not put it on a slide you will publish.

## A friendly token fits in a smaller square

`river-cloud-3847` is sixteen characters where a link with a random key is ninety. The QR code is smaller and scans from further away, and the token can also be said aloud or typed. The transfer id and the key are both derived from the token in both browsers, so the server never maps a token to anything and never sees it.

The trade: there are 1,024,000,000 tokens, and anyone holding the ciphertext can try them offline at 600,000 PBKDF2 rounds each. A random 256-bit key cannot be tried. So a friendly token is for a link that expires, a file that is not worth that effort, and a moment when speaking it is the point; a random key is for everything else. The send page shows which you chose and the expiry you set.

## Scanning

This release draws codes; it does not scan them. A phone's camera app opens a scanned link in the browser, which is the common case. Scanning with the page's own camera is proposed and listed as such in [the reality file](/about/reality/).

## Compatibility

A link or a token made here opens on [send.sgraph.ai](https://send.sgraph.ai), and one made there opens on [the open page](/open/) here: the fragment grammar, the token derivations and the word list are the same, copied from the SG/Send repository and held by tests. [The contracts](https://api.send.sgit.ai/docs/contracts/) are written down on the API's site.


==============================================================================

# Security, what the server sees

> What the server can see, what it cannot, the two secrets that must not be confused, what a friendly token costs, and what this site does not claim.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/learn/security/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Security: what the server sees, and what it cannot

*As storyboards: [The envelope and the fragment](/storyboards/the-envelope/) and [What can go wrong](/storyboards/what-can-go-wrong/).*

## The server

| It can see | It cannot see |
|---|---|
| The ciphertext, and its size (the plaintext plus 28 bytes for a transfer) | The plaintext |
| When it was uploaded, and how many times it was downloaded | The file name: it is inside the ciphertext |
| A hash of the sender's IP, salted daily | The decryption key: it is in the link's fragment |
| The `content_type_hint` the sender chose | The vault key or the passphrase; it stores a hash of the write key and compares |
| Your access token, hashed, to decide whether you may upload | Who you sent the link to |

The server is a capability-checked ciphertext store: every access decision it makes is a hash comparison, and it never holds a raw key. A full compromise of it yields ciphertext and hashes. That property is the whole product rather than a feature of it, and [sgit.ai's security page](https://sgit.ai/security/) covers it from the server's side.

## This site

This site is static files on GitHub Pages: it has no way to receive a request body. The code the pages run comes from [api.send.sgit.ai](https://api.send.sgit.ai), pinned to one release whose every file is hashed in [the manifest](https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/manifest.json) and checked by this repository's gate. No script, style or font is loaded from any other origin. Nothing is stored except what you can see on [Keys](/keys/) and the theme you picked.

## Two secrets that must not be confused

The **access token** says who may upload. It goes in a request header to the server you chose and nowhere else: never a URL, never a log. The **decryption key** says who may read. It goes in the link after `#` or by a second channel, and never reaches any server. They are unrelated values. Confusing them does not throw an error, which is why it is the first thing on [the quick start](https://api.send.sgit.ai/start/).

## What a friendly token costs

A friendly token is two words from a list of 320 and four digits: 1,024,000,000 possibilities. Anyone holding the ciphertext can try them offline, at 600,000 PBKDF2 rounds each. That is a real cost, and it is not the cost of a random 256-bit key. A friendly token is for a link that expires and a file that is not worth that effort; a random key is for the rest. The send page says which you chose.

## The keyring

The keyring on [Keys](/keys/) is plaintext in your browser's storage. It makes the keys findable, which is what was missing before; it does not make them safe from someone with your device. Export it to a password manager for the keys that matter. [Vaults and keys](/learn/vaults-and-keys/) says where each kind of key should live.

## What this site does not claim

- **Not proved against the hosted server yet.** The formats match send.sgraph.ai's published contracts and the code is tested against an in-memory implementation of its API; a round trip against `send.sgraph.ai` itself is marked proposed in [the reality file](/about/reality/) until it is recorded.
- **Not audited.** The crypto is the browser's Web Crypto API, used the same way send.sgraph.ai has since its first version; nobody outside the project has reviewed this site's use of it.
- **Not metadata-free.** Sizes, timing and counts are visible to the server, and the link is as private as the channel it travels by.
- **A beta.** Do not upload confidential or illegal content.


==============================================================================

# Vaults and keys

> What a vault is, the one secret and the keys derived from it, which may be shared and which never, where each kind of key should live, and what to do when one is lost.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/learn/vaults-and-keys/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Vaults and keys

*As storyboards: [A folder that remembers](/storyboards/a-folder-that-remembers/) and [Where the keys live](/storyboards/where-the-keys-live/).*

## What a vault is

A vault is a folder of files, encrypted in your browser, versioned like git: every change is a commit, the history is kept, two devices can work on it and merge, and a laptop can `sgit clone` it. send.sgraph.ai had transfers; what it did not have, and what stopped people, was a place to keep the vault keys and a way to put files into vaults from the page. This site has both.

## One secret, and the keys derived from it

| Key | What it carries | Looks like | May be shared |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The vault key** | read and write | `sgit_private_vault_<passphrase>:<vault id>` | **never**: not in a link, a page, a chat, a repository |
| **The read key** | read only, every file, every version | `sgit_public_read_<64 hex>:<vault id>` | yes: this is what a share link carries |
| **The write key** | what the server checks before accepting a push | never shown; derived from the passphrase, sent as a header, stored as a hash | no |

The read key is derived from the vault key one way, so a read key can never be turned back into write access. The vault id after the colon is the address, and it is public. [sgit.ai's credentials page](https://sgit.ai/docs/credentials.html) has the prefixes and why the word in them matters.

## Where each kind of key should live

| Key | Today, on this site | The better home |
|---|---|---|
| Vault keys | [Keys](/keys/), plaintext, per device; export to move | a password manager; [secrets.sgit.ai](https://secrets.sgit.ai)'s passkey-unlocked keyring when it ships; a registry vault fed over an append lane, as [sgit.ai's key management page](https://sgit.ai/docs/key-management.html) describes |
| Read keys | Keys, and in the links you hand out | anywhere; they are publishable |
| Transfer keys | Keys, with the delete secret | the same; they expire with the transfer |
| Access tokens | Keys, per server | a password manager |

## When a key is lost

There is no reset. A vault whose vault key is lost cannot be written to again; if a read key survives it can still be read and cloned, and its contents copied into a new vault. A transfer whose key is lost is gone. This is the price of the server never holding a key, and it is why the keyring exists: a key that is written down somewhere is a key that is not lost.

## When a key leaks

A read key that leaks means the vault's contents are as public as wherever it went; revocation is not retroactive, because anyone who fetched the objects keeps them. A vault key that leaks means rotating: make a new vault, copy the files, re-share the new read key, and stop using the old one. [Keys](/keys/) can revoke a transfer, which deletes it on the server, if the transfer was sent from this device.

## sgit, on a laptop

```
pip install sgit-ai
sgit clone sgit_public_read_…:vaultid        # read-only, every file and every commit
sgit clone sgit_private_vault_…:vaultid      # read and write
sgit commit "added the report" && sgit push  # then open it here again: the browser and the CLI are two clones of one vault
```

[sgit.ai](https://sgit.ai) is the documentation for the CLI and the vault format.

# Open

Everything that unlocks a file is after the `#` in the link, which your browser never sends to any server. Paste a link, a friendly token, or a read key; the file is decrypted here.

A link, a token, or a key

Open Nothing you paste here is uploaded.

## What this page can open

Looks likeIt isWhat happens

`#abc123def456/`43 charactersa transfer with its keydownloaded, decrypted here, saved with the name that was inside the ciphertext

`#abc123def456`a transfer, link onlythis page asks for the key that travelled separately

`#river-cloud-3847`a friendly tokenthe transfer id and the key are both derived from the token, here

`#sgit_public_read_…:vaultid`a vault's read keyevery file and every version, read only, decrypted here; also `sgit clone`-able

`#sgit_private_vault_…:vaultid`a vault keyopens too, with a warning: it is write access and should not have travelled in a link

A link made on [send.sgraph.ai](https://send.sgraph.ai) opens here too, and the other way round: the formats are the same. [QR codes and friendly tokens](/learn/qr-codes/).

# Settings

The server

The SG/Send API host that stores ciphertext. The hosted one is `send.sgraph.ai`; [you can run your own](https://sgit.ai/deploy/), or [one on this machine](/use/#local) for trying things out.

Host

Access token for that server

Sent as a request header to that host only, never in a URL, kept in [your keys](/keys/). This is the beta gate: [how to get one](/use/pricing/).

# Send, as storyboards

> How send.sgit.ai works, drawn: for everyone, the four things a person does (send a file, say a token aloud, keep files in a vault, keep the keys); under the hood, what the bytes look like, the two kinds of API, how an agent hands a result over, and what can go wrong. Each board links to the page where you can do it for real.

8 storyboards, 69 panels, drawn by the kit at api.storyboards.sgit.ai v0.1.0.

## For everyone

No cryptography required: what you do, what the other person sees, and what the server never sees.

- [Send a file. Keep the key.](/storyboards/send-a-file/index.md): Maya sends forty photos to Hugo, who has no account; the server keeps bytes it cannot read; Hugo scans a code on his phone. 9 panels.
- [A token you can say aloud](/storyboards/say-it-aloud/index.md): river-cloud-3847 is the whole key: Maya says it on a call, Hugo types it, Eve hears it a week too late. 8 panels.
- [A folder that remembers](/storyboards/a-folder-that-remembers/index.md): Ravi gets a new version every week; Maya puts the files in a vault, shares the read key once, and every version stays. 9 panels.
- [Where the keys live](/storyboards/where-the-keys-live/index.md): The thing that was missing before: a keyring on the device, what it is, what it is not, and the one rule about which key may travel. 8 panels.

## Under the hood

For the engineer and the agent: the bytes, the two APIs, a hand-over by an agent, and the six ways it fails.

- [The envelope and the fragment](/storyboards/the-envelope/index.md): What the bytes look like, which of them the server sees, and where each of the two secrets goes. 9 panels.
- [Two kinds of API](/storyboards/two-kinds-of-api/index.md): The code a page runs is a release that never changes; the server it talks to is a deployment. Inês pins one and runs the other. 8 panels.
- [An agent hands over](/storyboards/an-agent-hands-over/index.md): Pip finishes a job, sends the result once with an expiry, keeps the work in a vault, and never logs a key. 9 panels.
- [What can go wrong](/storyboards/what-can-go-wrong/index.md): Six ways a hand-over fails: a link in a public channel, expired, the wrong key, a vault key in a link, and what revocation does and does not do. 9 panels.

## The cast

The cast of send.sgit.ai's storyboards, v0.1, proposed by the site's build agent on 20 October 2026 for Dinis to accept, change or replace. Drawn by the storyboard kit at api.storyboards.sgit.ai from 'look'; nothing here is an image. Fictional people and agents, each standing for a part a person or an agent plays when a file is handed over: the sender, the recipient on a phone, the client who asks who else can see it, the engineer who embeds the code and runs her own server, the listener on the wire, the server that holds bytes it cannot read, and a session agent that hands over a result. Names chosen not to clash with the gen-z-developers or the pki casts. Eve is the name cryptography has long given a passive eavesdropper.

- **Maya** (she/her): the sender: a consultant who sends reports and photos to people who have no account anywhere. anyone with a file to hand over who should not have to learn cryptography to do it. "Scan this."
- **Hugo** (he/him): the recipient: on the newest phone he has ever owned, with no account and no wish for one. everyone a link is sent to who did not choose the site. "Do I need an account?"
- **Ravi** (he/him): the client: a finance director who receives a new version every week and asks who else can see it. the person who needs the latest version and an answer about who can read it. "Who else can see this?"
- **Inês** (she/her): the engineer: embeds the send code in her company's product and runs a server of their own. anyone who builds on this and must know exactly which code their readers run. "Which release is this page running?"
- **Eve** (they/them): the listener: on the wire, in the chat, by the laptop; reads whatever passes and never gets the key. every channel a link travels by, and every reason the key must not travel with it. "Everything after the # is yours, not mine."
- **The Server** (it/its): the server: a capability-checked store of ciphertext, at send.sgraph.ai or wherever it is deployed. what a zero-knowledge service is: it holds the bytes, checks hashes, and cannot read anything. "I keep the bytes. I cannot read them."
- **Pip** (it/its): a session agent: a Claude session that finishes a job, hands the result over once, and keeps the work in a vault. every agent that must hand something to a person or another agent without an account and without pasting a key. "Report ready. One link, seven days."

Source: learn/qr-codes/index.md

## 6. On Hugo's phone
- **Hugo** (think, confused): "Do I need an account?"
- **Maya** (wave, happy): "No. The key is in the link."
- prop: phoneqr, send.sgit.ai/open/#…

Note: Opening needs nothing: no token, no account. The key is the gate.
Source: open/index.html

## 7. Decrypted on his phone
- **Hugo** (arms-up, happy): "There they are."
- prop: phone
- prop: mark, decrypted here

Note: Download, decrypt, unwrap: the file and its name come back in Hugo's browser, byte for byte.
Source: open/index.html

## 8. What the server is (evidence)
> The server is a capability-checked ciphertext store: every access decision it makes is a hash comparison, and it never holds a raw key.
> (learn/security/index.md)
- The Server, stand, calm

Note: Quoted from the security page, word for word.

# The envelope and the fragment

> What the bytes look like, which of them the server sees, and where each of the two secrets goes. 9 panels.

*Send, as storyboards · Under the hood · board 05 · built · send.build, 20 October 2026. The script of a storyboard drawn by the kit at api.storyboards.sgit.ai; the data is storyboard.json and bundle.json beside this file.*

## 2. The name goes inside
- **Inês** (point, determined): "Wrapped before encrypting. Get the order wrong and the download has no name."
- prop: board, SGMETA\0           7 bytes / meta_len           4 bytes, big-endian / {"filename": "report.pdf"} / file bytes         the rest

Note: The SGMETA envelope, the layout send.sgraph.ai has used since its first version.

## 3. Then AES-256-GCM
- Inês, stand, happy

Source: learn/index.md

## 4. Two secrets, two places
- **Inês** (point, determined): "Never the other way round."
- prop: key, access token: a request header
- prop: key, decryption key: the # fragment

Note: The token says who may upload; the key says who may read. Confusing them does not throw.
Source: learn/security/index.md

## 5. What the server sees
- **The Server** (stand, calm): "Bytes, a size, a time, a hint you chose."
- prop: server, send.sgraph.ai
- prop: board, ciphertext, size, time / a hashed IP / content_type_hint / not: name, key, plaintext

Note: The full list, both columns, is on the security page.
Source: learn/security/index.md

## 6. Eve on the wire
- **Eve** (shrug, thinking): "Everything after the # is yours, not mine."
- prop: arrow, #id/key never leaves the browser
- prop: padlock, fragment

Note: A browser never sends the fragment of a URL to the server that serves the page.
Source: learn/index.md

## 7. The token, in one place (evidence)
> The access token says who may upload. It goes in a request header to the server you chose and nowhere else: never a URL, never a log.

- Inês, point, determined

# Examples, a page, curl, Python

> The same transfer made three ways: from a page with the pinned API, from a shell with curl and openssl, and from Python for an agent; plus the server in memory for trying it on a laptop.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/use/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Use it: examples

Everything here talks to the same server with the same formats, so a file sent one way opens every other way, including on [the open page](/open/).

## From a page {#page}

```html
<script type="module">
  import * as send from 'https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js'
  const api = new send.SendTransfers({ endpoint: 'https://send.sgraph.ai', accessToken })
  const r   = await api.send({ bytes, filename: 'report.pdf', expiresAt: Date.now() + 7 * 86400e3 })
  const url = send.link.transferLink({ openUrl: 'https://send.sgit.ai/open/', transferId: r.transferId, key: r.keyString })
  qr.innerHTML = send.qr.toSvg(url)
</script>
```

Full walk-through, including a friendly token and a vault: [the quick start](https://api.send.sgit.ai/start/).

## From a shell, with curl and openssl {#curl}

The layout is simple enough to do by hand: envelope, encrypt, three calls.

```bash
TOKEN=...; HOST=https://send.sgraph.ai; FILE=report.pdf
KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32); IV=$(openssl rand -hex 12)
META=$(printf '{"filename":"%s"}' "$FILE"); LEN=$(printf '%s' "$META" | wc -c)
{ printf 'SGMETA\0'; printf "$(printf '\\x%02x\\x%02x\\x%02x\\x%02x' $((LEN>>24&255)) $((LEN>>16&255)) $((LEN>>8&255)) $((LEN&255)))"; printf '%s' "$META"; cat "$FILE"; } > plain.bin
# AES-256-GCM: openssl's CLI cannot emit the GCM tag; use the Python example below for GCM, or sgit's transfer command when it ships.
```

A GCM tag is required, and OpenSSL's command line does not produce one, so the honest shell example stops here: the three HTTP calls are below in Python, and they are the same from curl.

```bash
ID=$(curl -s -H "x-sgraph-access-token: $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"file_size_bytes":1234,"content_type_hint":"application/octet-stream"}' $HOST/api/transfers/create | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["transfer_id"])')
curl -s -H "x-sgraph-access-token: $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/octet-stream' --data-binary @cipher.bin $HOST/api/transfers/upload/$ID
curl -s -X POST -H "x-sgraph-access-token: $TOKEN" $HOST/api/transfers/complete/$ID
echo "https://send.sgit.ai/open/#$ID/$KEY_BASE64URL"
```

## From Python, for an agent {#python}

An agent that finishes a job and hands the result over once. Standard library plus `cryptography`; no account for the recipient.

```python
import base64, json, os, struct, urllib.request
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM

HOST, TOKEN = 'https://send.sgraph.ai', os.environ['SGRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN']   # the token: an env var, a header, never a URL

def send_file(path, expires_ms=0, max_downloads=0):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    meta = json.dumps({'filename': os.path.basename(path)}).encode()
    plain = b'SGMETA\0' + struct.pack('>I', len(meta)) + meta + data          # the name inside the ciphertext
    key, iv = AESGCM.generate_key(256), os.urandom(12)
    cipher = iv + AESGCM(key).encrypt(iv, plain, None)                        # IV || ciphertext || tag
    def call(method, p, body=None, ctype='application/json'):
        req = urllib.request.Request(HOST + p, data=body, method=method, headers={'x-sgraph-access-token': TOKEN, 'content-type': ctype})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r: return r.read()
    tid = json.loads(call('POST', '/api/transfers/create', json.dumps({'file_size_bytes': len(data), 'content_type_hint': 'application/octet-stream', 'max_downloads': max_downloads, 'expires_at': expires_ms}).encode()))['transfer_id']
    call('POST', f'/api/transfers/upload/{tid}', cipher, 'application/octet-stream')
    call('POST', f'/api/transfers/complete/{tid}')
    k = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(key).decode().rstrip('=')
    return f'https://send.sgit.ai/open/#{tid}/{k}'                             # the key: in the fragment, never logged

def receive(link):
    frag = link.split('#', 1)[1].split('|')[0]; tid, k = frag.split('/', 1)
    key = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(k + '=' * (-len(k) % 4))
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f'{HOST}/api/transfers/download/{tid}') as r: cipher = r.read()   # public: the key is the gate
    plain = AESGCM(key).decrypt(cipher[:12], cipher[12:], None)
    assert plain[:7] == b'SGMETA\0'; n = struct.unpack('>I', plain[7:11])[0]
    return json.loads(plain[11:11 + n])['filename'], plain[11 + n:]
```

For an agent-facing link prefer `max_downloads=0` with a short `expires_ms`: a retry is not a reader, and a cap burns the allowance. [For agents](/use/agents/) has the rest of that guidance.

## On a laptop, with the server in memory {#local}

```
git clone https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Send__API
node SGit-AI__Website__Send__API/releases/v0.1.1/tests/server.mjs 8787 local-dev-token
```

Then in [Settings](/settings/) choose "a server on this machine" with the token `local-dev-token`. Every feature works, nothing leaves the machine, and it forgets everything when it stops. It is the same server the API's 43 tests run against.


==============================================================================

# For agents

> How an agent sends a result to a person or to another agent with these formats, what to put in the bundle, which secrets go where, and the pages to read first.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/use/agents/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# For agents

*As a storyboard: [An agent hands over](/storyboards/an-agent-hands-over/).*

You are reading the page for agents of send.sgit.ai. Every page here has a markdown twin at the same path with `.md` instead of `.html`; [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) lists them, and [`/llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) is all of them in one request. The code this site runs has [its own agents page](https://api.send.sgit.ai/agents/).

## Handing a result over, once

A transfer is the right shape when a job finishes and the result goes to someone once: a report, a bundle, a dated export. [The Python example](/use/#python) is the whole thing in forty lines; the formats are [the contracts](https://api.send.sgit.ai/docs/contracts/). Three rules, from [sgit.ai's transfer page](https://sgit.ai/api/transfers.html):

- **The access token is a header, from an environment variable or a secret store.** Never in a URL, a log line, or a transcript.
- **The decryption key is in the link, and nowhere else.** Do not persist it in node output or a tool result that is kept.
- **Prefer a time bound to a download cap** for a link another agent will open: `max_downloads: 0` with a short `expires_at`, because a retry is not a reader.

Bundle for a reader who is an agent: a `manifest.json` saying what each file is and an `llms.txt` cost nothing and are the difference between a payload that can be used and one that has to be opened by a person first.

## Working in a vault, repeatedly

A vault is the right shape when the thing is read repeatedly, updated, or browsed: use `sgit` ([the skill is on sgit.ai](https://sgit.ai/skills/)) with the vault key you were given, commit, push, and hand the **read key** to whoever should see it. Never paste a vault key into a chat; [sgit.ai's key management page](https://sgit.ai/docs/key-management.html) has the flow that sends one to a registry sealed to its public key instead.

## From a browser agent

The pinned release runs in any page: `import('https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js')`, then `SendTransfers.send()` and `receive()`, or the `vault` namespace. Opening needs no token.

## What to read first

1. [The reality file](/about/reality/): what exists on this site. If it is not there, it does not exist.
2. [Security: what the server sees](/learn/security/).
3. [The API's agents page](https://api.send.sgit.ai/agents/) and [its reality file](https://api.send.sgit.ai/about/reality/).


==============================================================================

# Embed it in your site

> Put a send box, an open page, or a QR hand-over on your own site by pinning the same release this site runs; what to pin, what to check, what stays on your origin.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/use/embed/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Embed it in your site

The code this site runs is not this site's. It is [api.send.sgit.ai](https://api.send.sgit.ai) v0.1.1, and any page on any origin can import it the same way:

```html
<script type="module">
  import * as send from 'https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js'
</script>
```

A script loaded from that host runs on **your** page's origin, so the keyring, the clone branch and everything the modules store stay in your site's storage; the API host has no way to receive anything. The three things to get right:

1. **Pin the release** in one file and copy its [manifest](https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/manifest.json) beside it; make your build refuse a reference to the host that is not that release. This site does it in `tools/api.json` and `tools/check.py`.
2. **Keep the access token out of the page.** It belongs to whoever uploads, in their browser, pasted once into something like [Settings](/settings/). A token in page source is a token everyone has.
3. **Build the link on your open page.** `send.link.transferLink({ openUrl: 'https://your.site/open/', ... })`, and parse it there with `send.link.parseFragment(location.hash)`. Or point at `https://send.sgit.ai/open/`, which opens anything made with these formats.

This site's own app modules (`assets/app/send.js`, `open.js`, `vaults.js`, `keys.js`, `settings.js`) are small, plain ES modules with no framework; copy the ones you want from [the repository](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Send) and keep the import of the pinned release. [For developers](https://api.send.sgit.ai/for-developers/) on the API's site has the per-module notes and what runs in Node.


==============================================================================

# The commercial model

> How using this site and its capabilities is meant to be paid for, what is true today (a beta behind access tokens), what is proposed, and what will never be charged for.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/use/pricing/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# The commercial model

The brief for this site [says it plainly](/about/brief/#memo-02): the point is a full usage-based commercial model for using the site and its capabilities. This page is that model, with the status of every part marked, because most of it is not built yet.

## Today, counted {#today}

| | Status |
|---|---|
| **Opening a link** is free, needs no account and no token, and always will. The key is the gate | shipped |
| **Sending** needs an access token, issued by hand during the beta. A token has a use limit and can be revoked | shipped (the gate exists on the server; tokens are made by a person) |
| **How to get a token:** write to the address at the bottom of this page with what you want to send and how often | shipped, by email |
| **Running your own server** with the open-source SG/Send API, and pointing [Settings](/settings/) at it: no token from us, no bill from us | shipped |
| **Embedding the code** from api.send.sgit.ai in your own site: free, Apache-2.0 | shipped |

## Proposed {#proposed}

Each row is described in a brief and has no code behind it on this site. The reality file lists them as proposed; nothing here is a promise.

| Idea | Shape |
|---|---|
| **Self-service tokens** | pay for an allowance of uploads or bytes, get a token in the browser, keep it in [Keys](/keys/) |
| **Usage meter on the page** | the token's remaining uses shown on the send page, as the API already reports them |
| **Vault hosting** | a vault above a size or an age carries a cost, paid by its owner, with the read key free to everyone who holds it |
| **Organisations** | a token per team with its own servers or its own bucket, under their own keys |
| **A reading meter for shared content** | the newsroom's [SG Meter](https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai) pattern applied to a vault page: pay by how far you read, in the browser |

## What will not be charged for {#never}

- Opening a link, ever. The recipient did not choose this site.
- Reading a vault with its read key, or cloning it with sgit.
- Exporting your keys, or leaving: there is no account to close and nothing of yours on this site.
- The code: api.send.sgit.ai is open source and stays so.

## How to get an access token today

Write to [agent@riskmandate.ai](mailto:agent@riskmandate.ai) with what you want to send and how often. During the beta tokens are issued by hand and use-limited; a token is tied to a server, kept in your browser, and sent only in a request header to that server.


==============================================================================

# Vaults

> The vaults this browser holds keys for. Create one, add files as commits, see the history, and share it read-only with a link and a QR code; clone it anywhere with sgit.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/vaults/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.4 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Vaults

A vault is a folder of files, encrypted here, versioned like git, that you can open again, add to, and share read-only. The vault key stays on this device; the read key is the one you hand out. Anyone with the read key can also `sgit clone` it on a laptop.

**Beta:** creating and writing to a vault needs an access token; [set one in Settings](/settings/). Opening a read key needs nothing.

## On this device

Create a vault

 Create

## How a vault differs from a transfer

TransferVault

Shapeone file, uploaded oncea versioned tree of files

Historynone; there is no second versioncommits, with messages

The reader getsthe whole file, or nothingany single file, without the rest

Lifecycleexpires, caps downloads, can be revokedlives until deleted

The credentiala key in the linka read key, derived one way from the vault key

Reach for it whena thing is handed over oncea thing is read repeatedly, updated, or browsed

[Vaults and keys](/learn/vaults-and-keys/), in full.

# Version history

Every change that lands on `dev` is a version, in `tools/version.json`, tagged by the deploy and shown in the header of every page. The code the app runs has [a history of its own](https://api.send.sgit.ai/versions/).

| Version | Date | Kind | What changed, and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **v0.1.4** | 2026-10-20 | feature | **Send, as storyboards: eight boards on two shelves, drawn in the browser by the storyboard kit.** A storyboards section, the technique and the format storyboards.sgit.ai's: a cast of seven (Maya, Hugo, Ravi, Inês, Eve, the Server, Pip), four boards for everyone (send a file, say it aloud, a folder that remembers, where the keys live) and four under the hood (the envelope, two kinds of API, an agent hands over, what can go wrong), 69 panels, each board as JSON with its bundle and its script, a shelf with covers drawn live, every panel on one page and the model sheet. The kit is api.storyboards.sgit.ai v0.1.0, pinned with the integrity string of every file, and the gate refuses any other reference. The build checks the cast, the vocabulary, every evidence quote word for word against the page it names, and every try-it link; the test runs the kit's own validator and draws every board in Chromium. |
| **v0.1.3** | 2026-10-20 | docs | **an article records the naming rule for the two kinds of API.** From a conversation with Dinis after the first deploy: api.<site>.sgit.ai is a site's client code, released as files; <service>.api.sgit.ai is a server, one deployment of a service's HTTP contract, with the environment leftmost; the first services are send and vault, split along the route prefixes the current server already has, with send.sgraph.ai becoming a router by prefix. A decision, not a deployment: nothing a page runs changed. |
| **v0.1.2** | 2026-10-20 | fix | **the pin check leaves articles alone.** v0.1.1 landed with the gate red on one line: the agent's article about the first release names the v0.1.0 address it was written against, and the pin check read that as an unpinned reference. An article is the record of its day, so the check now skips /articles/; nothing a page runs changed. Recorded here rather than hidden, as the release discipline asks. |
| **v0.1.1** | 2026-10-20 | fix | **the site pins api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1, whose health check asks the route the hosted service serves.** After the first deploy, Settings reported send.sgraph.ai as not answering: the v0.1.0 release asked /api/health, which the hosted service does not serve (its route is /api/info/health). The API's v0.1.1 fixes that; this version changes the pin and copies its manifest, and nothing else on the site. The same run measured that send.sgraph.ai allows requests from this origin with every header the release sends. |
| **v0.1.0** | 2026-10-20 | release | **the first version of send.sgit.ai: send, open, vaults, keys and settings on the pinned API, with the explanations, the examples, the commercial model and three articles.** From the four voice memos of 20 October 2026, published in full with their corrections. The app runs api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.0, pinned with its manifest: a file sent as a transfer or into a vault, a link, a friendly token or a QR code to hand over, an open page for any of them, vaults created and shared read-only, and a keyring on the device. An end-to-end browser test drives all of it against the in-memory server. What is not built is listed as proposed in the reality file, including the round trip against the hosted send.sgraph.ai. |
